Restate only the main (public) question.
Compute \(28 \times 40 + 16 \times 29\).

First, calculate \(28 \times 40\):
\[28 \times 40 = 1120.\]

Next, calculate \(16 \times 29\):
\[16 \times 29 = 16 \times (30 - 1) = 16 \times 30 - 16 \times 1 = 480 - 16 = 464.\]

Now, add the results of the two multiplications:
\[1120 + 464 = 1584.\]

To double-check the main result, let's try an alternative order of operations:
First, calculate \(16 \times 29\) again as \(464\) (already done).
Then, calculate \(28 \times 40\) again as \(1120\) (already done).
Finally, add these results:
\[1120 + 464 = 1584.\]

The answer to the main question is \(1584\).
